title: Drug markets are changing while harm, treatment access, and enforcement pathways remain uneven across regions
source_unit: UNODC, World Drug Report 2026 data portal
geography: Global drug cultivation, health-harm, treatment, and market reporting across regions and subregions

observations.period: 2024-2026; illicit crop cultivation and market geography

cannabis_scope.unit: countries reporting cannabis cultivation, covering approximately 96 percent of the global population

coca_area.unit: hectares of illicit coca-bush cultivation in 2024

coca_change.unit: times the illicit coca cultivation area approximately a decade earlier

observations.method: UNODC compilation of illicit-crop cultivation, market, and country reporting in the World Drug Report 2026 data portal.
observations.uncertainty: Cultivation estimates depend on remote sensing, field reporting, definitions, and coverage; area is not equivalent to output, purity, retail availability, or consumption.
observations.subgroup: Communities in cultivation and transit areas, people exposed to organized crime or enforcement, farmers, consumers, and public-health systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Changes in cultivation area can reflect yields, eradication, policy shifts, displacement of production, or reporting changes rather than a simple increase in demand.

denominator.unit: countries and global indicators reporting drug-related deaths

global_death_trend.value: total global deaths directly or indirectly attributable to drugs continued to increase in 2023

population_adjustment.value: population-adjusted rates grew more slowly than total deaths

toxicology.value: among 66 reporting countries, opioids were the most common substance involved in direct drug-related deaths and cocaine ranked second

observations.method: UNODC synthesis of mortality, toxicology, and country reporting data.
observations.uncertainty: Mortality attribution and toxicology coverage vary across countries; indirect causes and underreporting mean direct counts do not capture the full burden.
observations.subgroup: People with drug use disorders, families, people using multiple substances, emergency and health workers, and communities with unequal access to care.
observations.counterinterpretation: Slower population-adjusted growth and regional declines in particular substances can coexist with severe local epidemics and changing drug mixtures.

denominator.unit: people with drug use disorders in countries with available treatment data

coverage.value: only a small proportion of people with drug use disorders receive treatment

regional_gradient.value: coverage is highest in Europe and lowest in Africa and Asia

service_variation.value: availability, coverage, and accessibility vary across pharmacological, psychosocial, and rehabilitation interventions

observations.method: UNODC synthesis of treatment-coverage and service-availability data in the World Drug Report 2026.
observations.uncertainty: Treatment estimates are limited by incomplete country reporting, differing definitions of treatment, and missing people outside formal services.
observations.subgroup: People with drug use disorders, women and youth, people in poverty, people in criminal-justice contact, and populations in under-resourced health systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal treatment coverage understates informal, community, peer, or self-managed recovery routes, while not all formal services have equal quality or accessibility.

observations.period: 2026; pathways into treatment and institutional response

denominator.unit: countries contributing data on referral pathways into drug-related treatment

referral_variation.value: friends and family or self-referral are more common in Africa, while criminal-justice referral has a larger role in East and South-East Asia

intervention_data.unit: countries contributing data on types of treatment delivered

polydrug_use.value: between 40 and 50 percent of people in drug-related treatment are reported as polydrug users in available global data, with substantial regional variation

observations.method: UNODC comparative analysis of treatment referral, intervention, and patient-profile data.
observations.uncertainty: These are selective reporting frames, not representative samples of all people who use drugs; referral pathways may reflect institutional access as much as preference or need.
observations.subgroup: People seeking treatment, families, criminal-justice agencies, health providers, community organizations, and people with multiple-substance use.
observations.counterinterpretation: Criminal-justice referral can sometimes connect people to care, while self- or family referral can also be blocked by stigma, cost, distance, or service scarcity.

related_sources.claim: UNODC WDR 2026 searchable findings provide treatment, mortality, toxicology, cultivation, and market-detail context.
UNODC 2025 key findings provide prior-cycle context for synthetic markets, treatment gaps, and drug-related harms.

boundary: This record adds an aggregate drug-market, public-health, treatment-access, and institutional-response route. It is not an individual substance-use panel, clinical effectiveness study, respondent-level treatment record, or causal estimate of enforcement or drug-market policy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official UNODC World Drug Report 2026 data portal and searchable findings were reviewed; cultivation, mortality, treatment coverage, referral pathways, intervention, and polydrug claims were cross-checked.
